title: wythoffEdges silently rounds vertex entries beyond 2^53 on a Big board instead of returning them exactly or throwing EngineOverflow
location: packages/engine/src/wythoff.ts:175 (toNumber = Number(arith.toBig(x)), no safety check), used at wythoff.ts:195
claim: On a Big board (any finite board that is not a standard matrix, such as a relabelled type), wythoffEdges converts each bigint vertex entry to a JavaScript number with no check. Entries beyond 2^53 therefore come back as the nearest double. The same input on a SafeInt board throws EngineOverflow, and every other engine conversion of this kind (affine.ts:201, form.ts:74, heaps.ts:109) checks and throws.
expected: SPEC 5.4 lists wythoffEdges as 'exact', and E-1 requires exact integer arithmetic. Oracle: sorted(wythoff_edges([[2,-1],[-3,2]], [2**52+1, 0])) has entries ±13510798882111491 (for example the edge (-4503599627370497, 0) to (4503599627370497, -13510798882111491)). The engine must return those integers exactly or throw EngineOverflow, as it does on SafeInt (E-2).
observed: On fromAdjacency of C = [[2,-1],[-3,2]] (arith Big) with rings [2^52+1, 0], every edge carries 13510798882111492 where the oracle has 13510798882111491. The same rounding appears on relabelled B3 with rings [2^52+1, 3, 0]. No error is thrown. Not reachable from T10, which offers named SafeInt boards and rings up to RING_MAX; it affects the engine API.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the file: npm ci, then npx vitest run --root packages/engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-p4-01-wythoff-edges-rounded.test.ts. The test fails with 13510798882111492 against the oracle's 13510798882111491 in six edges. The search harness is packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-diff-wythoff-big.test.ts (needs python3).
specRef: SPEC.md 5.4, table 'Geometry', row wythoffEdges: 'exact'; SPEC.md 5.1 E-1 'Exact', E-2 (SafeInt throws EngineOverflow); oracle wythoff_edges (lie_games.py lines 764 to 781); CONTRACTS.md 2.4 wythoffEdges: Enumeration<[number[], number[]]>; decisions/P4-A1.md 'wythoffEdges items, order and truncation' ('entries converted to number') does not say what happens beyond 2^53.
proposedFix: In toNumber, throw EngineOverflow when Number(x) is not a safe integer (or when BigInt(Number(x)) !== x), as affine.ts and form.ts already do; the caller can then retry or refuse.

title: wythoffEdges returns entries past 2^53 rounded on a Big board instead of exact values or EngineOverflow
claim: On a board in Big arithmetic, wythoffEdges finds the edges exactly in bigint and then writes every entry through Number(), so an entry beyond 2^53 is returned with a wrong last digit and nothing is thrown.
expected: SPEC 5.4 lists wythoffEdges as 'exact', and E-2 says every board other than a named finite type is computed in Big so values stay exact. A value the contracted number[] cannot hold should throw EngineOverflow, as on SafeInt and as symbolicPlay does (decisions/RT-FIX-P3-engine.md). The oracle's wythoff_edges gives 9007199254740995.
observed: Board fromAdjacency([[0,1,1],[1,0,0],[1,0,0]]) (A3 numbered with its middle node first; arith Big; classify: finite), rings [4503599627370497, 4503599627370498, 0], cap 1000. Result: 18 edges, truncated false, no throw. Every entry that is ±9007199254740995 in the oracle (and in the engine's own fire on the same board) comes back as ±9007199254740996. For example, the oracle's edge [-4503599627370497,9007199254740995,4503599627370497]|[0,9007199254740995,-4503599627370497] is returned with 9007199254740996. No tool reaches this: T10 offers only named boards on SafeInt, with rings of at most 999999.
reproduction: From a checkout of b9b8504 plus the reproducer, in the repository root: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-wythoff-big.test.ts (python3 runs the oracle bridge redteam/RT-03/bridge.py). The test 'every edge equals the oracle' fails with the diff above. The cap tests in the same file pass.
specRef: SPEC.md 5.1 E-2; 5.4 row wythoffEdges ('exact'); CONTRACTS.md 2.4 phase 4 wythoffEdges; oracle wythoff_edges(C, rings)
proposedFix: In toNumber, throw EngineOverflow when Number(b) is not a safe integer (or when BigInt(Number(b)) !== b), as heaps.ts toSafeNumber and form.ts coroot already do.

title: symmetrizer, gram, cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard and every guarded function throw RangeError on a board with a road count beyond 2^53, where the oracle answers
location: packages/engine/src/classify.ts:105 and :117 (rat(C[i][j]) in symmetrizer), :130 (gram), reaching rational.ts:34 (toBigInt accepts safe integers only)
claim: fromAdjacency accepts any integer road count, and the moves work on the Big board it returns. But symmetrizer builds rationals from entries that are plain numbers, and rat() rejects integers beyond 2^53. So the form functions, cartanClass on an asymmetric board, classify and smallestNonfiniteSubboard throw RangeError 'the numerator ... is not a safe integer'. Every guarded function, through requireFinite and classify, throws RangeError instead of NotFiniteType. Since b85ac0f the symmetric board with the same count is classified (the shortcut skips the rationals), while the asymmetric one is not.
expected: Oracle on C = [[2,-2**53],[-1,2]]: symmetrizer [1, 9007199254740992]; gram [[2,-9007199254740992],[-9007199254740992,18014398509481984]]; cartan_class 'indefinite'; classify [{'nodes': [1, 2], 'kind': 'gcm', 'balanced': True, 'class': 'indefinite', 'name': None}]; smallest_nonfinite_subboard ([1, 2], 'indefinite'). On [[2,-1,0],[-2**54,2,-1],[0,-1,2]]: 'indefinite' and ([1, 2], 'indefinite'). SPEC 5.6: these functions work on gcm boards, and a finite-theory function throws NotFiniteType.
observed: RangeError: the numerator -9007199254740992 is not a safe integer, from symmetrizer, gram, cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard and coxeterNumber; '... -18014398509481984 ...' on the 3-node board. Links reject such entries, since urlCodec requires safe integers. T16 import calls resolveBoard (which classifies) before its 4-roads check, so its refusal reads 'the numerator ... is not a safe integer' instead of the editor-limit sentence. The cause predates b85ac0f; the symmetric shortcut made it inconsistent.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the file: npm ci, then npx vitest run --root packages/engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-p4-02-entries-beyond-2-53.test.ts. 7 tests fail with RangeError and 2 pass (the moves, and the symmetric control).
specRef: SPEC.md 5.6 second table (cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard, symmetrizer/gram on gcm boards; NotFiniteType for finite-theory functions off the finite types); SPEC 5.1 E-2 ('every other board ... uses Big'), E-11; oracle symmetrizer, gram, cartan_class, classify, smallest_nonfinite_subboard (lie_games.py lines 106 to 126, 1061 to 1077, 1229 to 1271).

title: orbitGraph's fast path hashes positions linearly mod 2^30: an orbit inside 2^30·Z^n becomes quadratic and takes 85 to 103 s at the worker cap of 100000
location: packages/engine/src/search.ts:146-147 (R[k] and the hash sum of entry times R[k] mod 2^30), chain walks at :198 and :218
claim: The residual fix of P3-RT-07-02 replaced the decimal-key Map with a hash that is a linear function of the entries mod 2^30. Every position of the orbit of a seed in 2^30·Z^n gets the same hash, so each lookup walks every earlier position and the search time grows with the square of the cap.
expected: The residual fix's decision says every result, order, cap and interface is unchanged and the change only makes the search faster. Lens section 6: a wait of more than a minute at a cap means the cap failed to bound the work. The generic loop on the same input takes 2.7 s at cap 100000.
observed: orbitGraph(boardFromName('E8'), [[2^30 in all 8 entries]], 'firing', 100000) took 85.5 s at load 4.4 and 103.3 s at load 13 to 16. The same call through the generic loop (a copy of the arithmetic object) took 2.7 s, and from (1,...,1) it took 0.5 s. At cap 40000: 20.3 to 20.7 s against 0.76 to 0.86 s (24 to 27 times). Both return the same items. The triangle from (2^30,0,0) at cap 100000 took 30.9 s against 0.14 s from (1,0,0). No tool reaches it: T4's 100000-position count seeds unit vectors, T2 stops at 2000, and T10 rings are at most 999999.
reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-hash.test.ts --silent=false. At cap 40000 the test prints the three times and fails because the fast path is more than 5 times slower than the generic loop.
specRef: SPEC.md 5.1 E-6 ('No function loops without a bound'); 5.6 row 'Positions in an enumeration in the worker' (100000); decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4); build-plan/red-team/RT-03-bounds-and-errors.md section 6 (a wait of more than a minute at a cap)
proposedFix: Mix each entry non-linearly before summing, for example a multiplicative xorshift of its low 32 bits and of floor(x / 2^32), so that a sublattice does not collapse into one bucket.
